uncited: *   **Input:** A volume dataset (potentially bricked), a clip object (proxy geometry) defining the focus region, and a camera view.

*   **Output:** A rendered image where the focus region is rendered with full detail and the context region is rendered with lower quality or different transfer function settings, separated by the clip object's depth bounds.
*   **Clip Object:** A proxy geometry (e.g., sphere, box) representing the focus region.
It must have defined front-facing and back-facing polygons.
*   **Clip Texture:** A high-resolution depth component texture.
It stores the depth values of the back-facing polygons of the clip object.
*   **Depth Buffer:** Standard framebuffer depth buffer.
The rendering is performed in four passes to exploit early-z rejection.
The volume slices are drawn in front-to-back order.
**Pass 1: Initialize Depth Buffer with Front Faces**
*   Render the front-facing polygons of the clip object into the depth buffer.
*   Draw all volume slices in front-to-back order.
This establishes the initial depth occlusion for the front part of the volume relative to the clip object's front boundary.
*   Render the back-facing polygons of the clip object.
*   Copy the resulting depth values from the depth buffer into the **Clip Texture**.
This texture now holds the depth threshold for the back boundary of the focus region.
**Pass 3: Render Front Half of Volume (Front to Center)**
*   Render the front-facing polygons of the clip object into the depth buffer again (to reset/initialize depth for this pass).
*   Draw volume slices from the front of the volume up to the center of the clip object.
*   **Fragment Shader Logic:** At the beginning of the fragment shader, read the corresponding back-face depth value from the **Clip Texture**.
If the fragment's depth is greater than the fetched clip texture value, terminate shader execution (discard fragment).
This ensures that only fragments inside the focus region (behind the front face but in front of the back face depth) are processed.
**Pass 4: Render Back Half of Volume (Center to Back)**
*   Render the back-facing polygons of the clip object into the depth buffer.
*   Draw volume slices from the center of the clip object to the back of the volume.

*   **Fragment Shader Logic:** Similar to Pass 3, read the front-face depth value (now stored in the clip texture, as roles are reversed) and discard fragments if their depth is greater than the fetched value.
This ensures only fragments inside the focus region are processed for the back half.
*   **Time Complexity:** Four passes over the volume slices.
The fragment shader performs a texture lookup and comparison, which is relatively cheap but adds overhead per fragment.
Implementation is more complex than simple clipping.
This method was developed as part of a focus and context interface for interactive volume rendering.
